content: The Pettenkofer School of Public Health at LMU Munich, Germany, contributed to the evidence synthesis team conducting systematic reviews on the effectiveness of parenting interventions. This team included Professor Frances Gardner, an expert in Child and Family Psychology from the Department of Social Policy and Intervention at Oxford University, United Kingdom. Other members from the same department at Oxford University included Ms. Sophia Backhaus, Ms. Moa Schafer, and Dr. Jamie Lachman. Professor GJ Melendez-Torres, specializing in Clinical and Social Epidemiology from the College of Medicine and Health at the University of Exeter, United Kingdom, also participated. Additionally, Ms. Wendy Knerr, a senior researcher from The Write Effect in Oxford, United Kingdom, contributed to the team. The reviews on INTEGRATE criteria for parenting interventions were led by Professor Frances Gardner from Oxford University. Dr. Yulia Shenderovich from Cardiff University’s Centre for Development, Evaluation, Complexity, and Implementation in Public Health Improvement, United Kingdom, and Dr. Amalee McCoy from Oxford University also contributed. Ms. Moa Schafer, Ms. Mackenzie Martin, and Ms. Roselinde Janowski, all from Oxford University, were part of this effort. Ms. Sheila Varadan from the Institute of Private Law at the University of Leiden, Netherlands, and Ms. Sophia Backhaus from Oxford University also participated. Professor Jane Barlow, an expert in evidence-based intervention and policy evaluation from Oxford University, and Professor Catherine Ward from the University of Cape Town, South Africa, were also involved. The guideline methodologists included Professor Eva Rehfuess and Dr. Ani Movsisyan, both methodologists from the Pettenkofer School of Public Health at LMU Munich, Germany. The Evidence Gap Map Team was led by Professor Frances Gardner from Oxford University, with contributions from Ms. Sophia Backhaus and Dr. Jamie Lachman, also from Oxford University. The External Review Group included Ms. Yvonne Agengo from the International Rescue Committee in New York, USA; Dr. Betzabe Butron Riveros from the Unit of Family, Health Promotion, and Life Course at PAHO/WHO, USA; Dr. Chandre Gould, a senior research fellow at the Institute for Security Studies in Pretoria, South Africa; Dr. Patty Leijten from the Research Institute for Child Development and Education at the University of Amsterdam, Netherlands; Bernadette Madrid from the Child Protection Unit at the University of the Philippines; and Dr. Greta Massetti, Branch Chief of the Field Epidemiology and Prevention Branch and Senior Epidemiologist in the Division of Violence Prevention at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, Georgia, USA. The guideline writer was Ms. Sophia Backhaus from the Department of Social Policy and Intervention at Oxford University, United Kingdom. The declarations of conflict of interest were managed by publishing the names and brief biographies of all proposed GDG (Guideline Development Group) members on the WHO Violence Prevention webpage for public consultation over 14 days. No comments were received during this period. GDG members were required to update their Declaration of Interest forms before each meeting, and verbal declarations of interest were solicited at the beginning of each GDG meeting. The declared interests of the GDG members are summarized in the documentation.
